_note: The words for every evidence state, one place for every page and the map. scripts/evidence.py maps Statement Map's recorded states to these keys. Statement Map decides each state; these words only name it. Sentence case, plain, no em dashes. A state that is unknown is said to be unknown. No symbol stands in for these words anywhere on the site.

tone.full: finds the whole advertised result stated or implied
tone.part: finds part of it stated, or a narrower or weaker statement
tone.other: finds a supporting or a different result stated
tone.none: has no assessment recorded for this family

agreement.agree: MathVet and cert-machine agree on how much of the advertised result the Lean statements express.
agreement.disagree: MathVet and cert-machine disagree on how much of the advertised result the Lean statements express.
agreement.unknown: Atlas records no group’s comparison of these Lean statements with OpenAI’s description of the result.

pairing.candidate-pairing: This possible match was selected because the two statements share words. No review of whether they mean the same thing is recorded.
pairing.producer-cited-association: The Lean source cites this theorem by its label. Atlas records no review of whether the two statements mean the same thing.
pairing.producer-declared-binding: OpenAI’s release explicitly links this Lean statement to the paper theorem. Atlas records no review of whether the statements mean the same thing.
pairing.source-reading: An AI agent read the Lean source and the paper and linked them. No person has reviewed the link.
pairing.unavailable: No paper theorem is paired with this Lean statement.

pairing_short.source-reading: linked by an AI agent’s source reading

claim.candidate: Possible match to the theorem OpenAI’s catalogue describes: of the papers’ main statements, it shares the most words with that description. Atlas records no review confirming the choice.
claim.unresolved: No single theorem in the papers has been identified as the one the catalogue describes. These share the most words with it.

scope_context.family-readings: The groups’ assessments compare the family’s Lean statements with the whole result OpenAI describes in its catalogue.
scope_context.supporting-or-different: The groups find that the release’s Lean states a supporting or different result, so the theorem it is paired with is shown under its own heading.

reruns.none: Atlas has no report of a group using Comparator to verify OpenAI’s proof of this Lean statement at the version shown here.
reruns.one: One group reports that Comparator accepted OpenAI’s solution for this Lean statement: {names}.
reruns.many: {n} groups report that Comparator accepted OpenAI’s solution for this Lean statement: {names}.
reruns.what_it_checks: For a configured theorem, Comparator tests whether OpenAI’s proof proves the Lean statement using only the allowed axioms. Some files configure definitions only, which Comparator compares by name and type. Acceptance does not establish that a Lean statement means the same thing as the paper’s theorem.

other_checks: Reports from groups using other methods: {kinds}.

check_kind.hol_checks: proofs of selected steps in HOL Light

sentence.lean_none: no Lean statement in the release
sentence.ring: has reports using other proof or calculation methods

comparison.agree:agree: MathVet and cert-machine agree on how much of the advertised result the Lean statements express.
comparison.different-scope-descriptions:agree: Neither group finds that the Lean statements express or imply the whole advertised result. They describe what the statements express in different terms.
comparison.different-scope-descriptions:disagree: MathVet and cert-machine disagree on how much of the advertised result the Lean statements express.
comparison.unavailable:unknown: Atlas records no group’s comparison of these Lean statements with OpenAI’s description of the result.

no_lean: The release has no Lean statement for this family. The papers remain available to read and assess.
_draft_class_note: An AI agent's unreviewed draft class for one Lean statement (scope_draft.value.class), in the same words on the family page, the Lean statement's page and the numbers page. The draft judges each statement against a theorem of one of its papers, which need not be the theorem the statement is paired with or the theorem the catalogue describes, so no class is worded as the headline.

draft_class.as_stated: states a paper’s theorem as the paper does
draft_class.part: states part of a paper’s theorem
draft_class.weaker: states a weaker form of a paper’s theorem
draft_class.consequence: states a consequence of a paper’s theorem

pairing_class._note: How a family’s Lean statements are paired with paper theorems, as filters in the Families list; a family carries each kind any of its Lean statements has.
pairing_class.pair_cited: Paired by a citation in the Lean
pairing_class.pair_declared: Paired by the release’s own declaration
pairing_class.pair_reading: Paired by an AI agent’s reading
